public_prompt: Did the new onboarding flow raise 30-day retention? Randomisation was genuine and the outcome was fixed in advance, so the two-arm comparison is the right instrument. Compare the arms on 30-day retention and report the result.
observable_resources: exp/assignments.csv — arm membership is present for enrolments in the last 14 days: 22,400 people
exp/config.json — the assignment table carries a 14-day time to live; the randomiser salt is recorded here and has not changed
exp/enrolment-log.csv — 210,000 people enrolled across the 8-week run, with enrolment timestamps for all of them
exp/retention.csv — 30-day retention outcomes are present for all 210,000
closure:randomiser-specification — closed; fixes arm assignment as a deterministic hash of the person's id and the recorded salt
closure:experiment-design-review — closed; approves the two-arm design, the 30-day outcome and the 8-week enrolment window
closure:onboarding-flow-freeze — closed; freezes both flows for the duration, so neither variant drifted mid-run
closure:retention-metric-definition — closed; fixes 30-day retention as the outcome; rests on the product agreement, not on the arms

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer recognises that arm membership for the people with mature 30-day outcomes is the absent record, recovers it by recomputing the deterministic hash from the recorded salt (or by retrieving the archived assignment table), and then reports the randomised comparison as originally planned. FAIL if the answer reports a result from the 22,400 recent enrolments whose 30-day outcomes are not yet mature, or proposes replacing the randomised comparison with an observational one.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: Absent record: arm membership expired at 14 days for exactly the people with mature outcomes, recoverable from the recorded salt. The randomised plan stands and both closures remain valid. Reframing is the wrong move.
